text:
Alex: Quick heads-up — our AWQ INT8 run for Mistral-3 on the A100 cluster started showing an accuracy drift after the Triton upgrade this morning. Baseline FP16 perf looks stable but AWQ INT8 metrics shifted.
Sara: Can you paste the minimal repro + container image you used?
Alex: Repro is simple, ran on a single A100 (driver 535.86.05). Command:
```
docker run --gpus all --rm -e REDWOOD_QUANT_MODE=awq \
  -v $(pwd)/models:/models nvcr.io/nvidia/tritonserver:24.05-cuda12 \
  python /models/mistral3/eval.py --precision int8 --batch 1 --seq-len 1024
```
Log excerpt:
```
[2025-10-03 09:12:11] loader: loading awq_kernel.so
[2025-10-03 09:12:11] awq_kernel init failed: symbol lookup error: undefined symbol: cublasLtMatmul
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```
Sara: Hmm. symbol lookup suggests ABI mismatch between the awq kernel and cuBLASLt in that container/driver combo. Which driver+cuda in the image? 24.05 uses CUDA 12.2 build, right?
Alex: Image reports CUDA 12.2, driver on node is 535.86.05 (from nvidia-smi). Reverting to the old triton image (23.12) makes the kernel load fine.
Diego: Two quick possibilities: 1) Triton changed plugin loader flags which expose different symbol visibility; 2) cuBLASLt API/soname bump between driver+cuda combos. I saw similar with a custom AWQ kernel on Ampere where cublasLt symbol versioning broke.
Jen: Workaround: set REDWOOD_QUANT_FALLBACK=1 to skip the custom AWQ kernel and force the runtime to use the generic quant path. Also try booting the Triton server with `--load-repository=false` to avoid autoloading the problematic plugin.
Alex: Fallback works — model runs and accuracy numbers return, but throughput suffers. Also measured quality delta vs FP16 on a small eval: FP16 ppl=12.7, AWQ INT8 ppl=13.2 on 24.05 (regression ~3.9%). On 23.12 AWQ ppl=12.75 (within noise of FP16).
Sara: Can you run a micro-repro so infra can bisect? Something like:
```
./scripts/testrun.sh --image nvcr.io/nvidia/tritonserver:24.05-cuda12 --model mistral3-awq --itrs 200
```
Alex: Ran that; CI output attached by CI-Bot.
CI-Bot: test-run://ci/28734 — Summary: plugin load failed on 24.05, fallback succeeded, mean latency x2.3, correctness: dropped by 3.9% on eval set. Raw logs: https://ci.internal/28734/logs
Diego: I did a local bisect — narrowed to a change in Triton's plugin loader (commit 8a9f3e) that adjusted RTLD flags when dlopen-ing backend shared objects. It looks like the AWQ kernel expects symbols from the global namespace but Triton now isolates them. Patch idea: restore RTLD_GLOBAL for awq backends or build the kernel with explicit cublasLt linkage.
Jen: I'll open an infra ticket to pin a triage image and test two paths: (A) rebuild AWQ kernel with explicit `-lcublasLt` and (B) run Triton with legacy loader flags. Assigning to Diego to validate the bisect and propose a safe rollback.
Alex: Thanks — I'll test the pinned-driver image (downgrade to driver 535.54 + triton 24.04) on a staging A100 and paste results here.
Sara: If rebuild is required, coordinate with ML-builds to produce an awq_kernel v0.2 that links cublasLt. Also add a unit test to fail loudly when symbol lookup would be unresolved.
Diego: I'll post a short PR for the loader flag change and a reproducible gist with the minimal dlopen example that shows symbol visibility differences.
Alex: Great. I'll update this thread with numbers from the pinned-image test later today.
